knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Only trained and authorised operators run the machine, after reading the manual and under supervision. Watching it run once (option 0) and carrying a passenger (option 2) are not acceptable.
The brushes are switched off and the parking brake set before anything is touched. Reaching under a running machine (option 0) and moving on (option 2) are unsafe.
The centre broom is stopped before the hopper is raised. Raising it while the broom turns (options 0 and 2) is a crush and strike hazard.

practicalCriteria: The learner completes a pre-operation check on a supplied machine covering the manual, controls, brakes, brushes, hopper, filter, lights and damage tags, and states whether the machine may be used; the assessor checks the record against the machine's condition.

The learner clears large objects from a supplied route, sets signs and cones, and starts the unit in the stated order: suction flap, brushes, parking brake freed, gentle acceleration; the assessor observes each step.

The learner shuts the machine down at the end of the run in the stated order, sets the parking brake, checks and cleans the filter, and empties the hopper before leaving the machine; the assessor confirms the engine is off before the learner walks away.
The learner states the stop-and-check response to a snagged object and demonstrates it on a supplied scenario; the assessor confirms the brushes are switched off and the parking brake set first.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Pre-operation check record for the machine
Operator authorisation record, as the business sets it
stopWorkCriteria: Learner operates the machine without a trained and authorised person in charge
Learner carries a passenger, or allows one to ride
Learner reaches under or into the brush while the machine is running
Learner lifts the hopper while the centre broom turns, or walks away from the unit with the motor still running
